object: cartouche at the end (?) of a line of Egyptian hieroglyphs on the back wall of a niche holding an altar
site: Naga, Temple f (the small temple)
notes: Meroitic HIEROGLYPHIC type, not cursive; read with Griffith's sign table (MI I p. 49), outside the tested cursive skill. Only the Meroitic cartouche is transcribed; the Egyptian words around it are not ('The royal cleansing (?) of the Son of Re, Lord of the Two Lands, Shanakazakhete, to whom life is granted for ever'). Column read top to bottom; in the side-by-side pair (reed, oval) the right-hand sign is read first, as the names in this volume require. Griffith: 'No one familiar with the inscriptions of the Meroites will fail to be struck by the comparative correctness of the inscription'; about the age of the Ammon temple, perhaps a little earlier. L., D., V., 68 d; Pl. XXIII.

object: square sandstone support, probably for a sacred bark, sculptured on each side (Berlin 7261)
site: Wad Ben Naga, the eastern (Isis) temple
notes: Meroitic HIEROGLYPHIC type, not cursive; read with Griffith's sign table (MI I p. 49), outside the tested cursive skill. Two Meroitic cartouches, the 'tiny bilingual keys' of Lepsius: the king's over his right shoulder on the west side (Griffith: 'Son of the Sun, Lord of diadems, Natakamani') and the queen's on the east side ('Daughter of the Sun, Lady of diadems, Amanitêre'). The Egyptian titles above them, the Egyptian prenomens (Kheper-ke-Re, Merkere) and the Egyptian columns are not transcribed. Columns read top to bottom, side-by-side signs right to left (king: owl over water to the right of the man, so m n i; queen: n i and r e). L., D., V., 55 a; Pls. XXIV-XXV.

object: wall inscription ('sur un mur d'enceinte', copied by Cailliaud)
site: Musawwarat es-Sufra
notes: Cursive type, archaic; Cailliaud, Voyage, Texte iii, Pl. 5 no. 3; LD VI 10 no. 50; Pl. XXVI. No dividers printed; the word space follows Griffith's comment ('made by Arkiwal (?) from Nakazy'; n?kdy occurs in 129/3; '-so' (his '/3') is an ending in many Philae graffiti). The '?' marks are Griffith's; he says n might be read for the first k. The final s checked at 3x against the table (rounded, not m or ẖ).

object: graffito (?)
site: Musawwarat es-Sufra
notes: Cursive type; LD VI no. 54; archaic. Griffith: 'The signs may be read ..., a name Tabakize'; the '?' on t and b are his.

object: inscription on the west (innermost) wall of the cella of the peripteral temple
site: Musawwarat es-Sufra
notes: Cursive type, late style; from P. Drummond's copy. Griffith: the first word is a man's title at Philae and Karanog, a name follows, then a descriptive phrase ending in -lo (as in no. 65). The m and both ẖ checked at 2.5x against the table (m narrow, ẖ wide and angular). The '?' on se and d are Griffith's.

object: sandstone stela on a large tall base, by a reservoir
site: Umm Soda (reservoir about 40 miles SE of Ba'sa)
text_std: [.][.][.][.][.] de[te] lḫte se : n # ke mlolḫte se : silw : detete tewi : e toẖetese : mkilw : de tetewi : e [toẖetese :]
notes: Cursive type, archaic. Griffith prints it 'divided and restored thus' in four lines with the stone's line numbers 2-11; line 1 is lost (his five dots). Brackets are his restorations: te in l. 2, and the end of l. 11 restored from ll. 8-9. '#' stands for a small zigzag sign set between two dots in Griffith's l. 4 (after n), not a letter of his alphabet and not explained by him; probably a numeral or measure, so it is not counted as a sign and is kept as '#' in both texts. Griffith: detelḫe occurs at Kalabsha (94/19); lḫte is probably the word in Soba no. 1; in ll. 7-8 'dete (:) tewi' is probably meant (dittography of te); yeto is found for ato 'water' in Kar. 107; mkilw (l. 10) occurs in Kar. 127; the text seems to refer to the water of the reservoir. The 3-shaped signs were checked at 2x against the table: m in mlolḫte and mkilw, s in silw, ẖ in toẖetese.

object: two cartouches engraved on the chest of a small sandstone lion
site: Ba'sa (reservoir with temple of the Lion-god, Wady Awatib)
notes: Meroitic HIEROGLYPHIC type, not cursive; read with Griffith's sign table (MI I p. 49), outside the tested cursive skill. Left cartouche: an Egyptian group 'Lord of the two lands', then Meroitic qor (Griffith: the title qêre without its final vowel), then three ankh signs (Egyptian; not transcribed). Right cartouche: mnḫble, Griffith's 'Mankhabale (or Amanikhabale)'. Sayce, PSBA 31; Pls. XXVI-XXVII.

object: round-topped sandstone stela from the shrine of the pyramid (Berlin 2253)
site: Meroe, pyramids in the plain (group C), Pyr. C 15
text_std: wosi : asoreyi : tkt?idmniqo : dokror : erkelo : amni terese : edḫli : edḫlo : atmlo : aḫrkte : amlol : ẖolkte : asi : asoreyi
notes: Cursive type, archaic, six printed lines. Griffith's translation: 'O Isis! O Osiris! behold me (?), the honoured (?) Taktizamani, begotten of Zêkarêr, born of Amanitares. All food be unto me (?). All things be given me (?). O Isis! O Osiris!'. He marks sic on aḫrkte, amlol (for ḫmlol) and asi (for wosi): the scribe begins almost every word of the closing formulae with a. His '?' marks the third letter of the name (t), which is unfinished on the stone. The ẖ of ẖolkte and the s of wosi and asi were checked at 2x against the table. Not in the corpus (no row shares its names), but T0801 is a close formula parallel ('woSi aSoreyi ... ato mlo ... at mlo ixrkte woSi aSoreyi').

object: spout broken from a table of offerings, dark sandstone (Berlin 2266)
site: Meroe, pyramids in the plain (group C) (Lepsius's label)
notes: Cursive type, late. Griffith prints no separate text: what survives is row '50' of his table of the royal formulae K, L, C on p. 82, aligned with nos. 59 and 60. Formula K is lost (dots only, not transcribed); this row gives L, then C. Each [.] is one of Griffith's dots for lost signs, not a measured count. He restores the stroke of the last te ('[/]<-'), marked te? here. He notes that the fragment also has part of the names of Isis and Osiris, which are not printed in type.

object: ink or incised labels on the north wall of the shrine (removed to Khartoum 1905)
site: Meroe, pyramids on the hills, Pyr. A 10
notes: Cursive type. (a) Five lines in front of the eleventh woman from the right; Griffith prints its text once, as the duplicate of 52 (b) ('51 a and 52 b are duplicates'): 'This seems to describe the woman as Bake, wife of a yere-bereke'. (b) Two lines in front of the next figure, apparently erased: [.]e and [.]qo (hatched = lost; 'with looped q'). Pl. XXIX.

object: inscriptions on the south wall of the shrine (British Museum 719)
site: Meroe, pyramids on the hills, Pyr. A 10
notes: Cursive type. (a) In front of the prince, 'almost illegible': o[.]yi (one hatched sign). (b) Three lines in front of a woman in the lowest row but one, the duplicate of 51 (a) (see there for Griffith's reading 'Bake, wife of a yere-bereke').

object: short inscription, 25 cm long (Lepsius's no. 29, squeeze in Berlin)
site: Meroe, pyramids on the hills, Pyr. A 10 (as published by Lepsius)
notes: Cursive type, 'an ancient style of writing'; nearly identical with no. 54. Griffith: 'The signs are difficult to identify'; the '?' on e and w are his.

object: short inscription, 18 cm long (Lepsius's no. 31, squeeze in Berlin)
site: Meroe, pyramids on the hills, Pyr. A 10 (as published by Lepsius)
notes: Cursive type, ancient style; nearly identical with no. 53. The last sign is hatched (lost). The '?' on o, ñ and s are Griffith's.

object: cartouche in front of the queen on the right-hand (northern) tower of the pylon of the shrine (red sandstone; Berlin 2245)
site: Meroe, pyramids on the hills, Pyr. A 15
notes: Meroitic HIEROGLYPHIC type, not cursive; read with Griffith's sign table (MI I p. 49), outside the tested cursive skill. A bare cartouche printed as one horizontal line and read right to left (the signs face the end of the line). Griffith: 'containing the name Amani-shakhetê, with the common suffix qo'; Cailliaud's sketch shows no signs above it. L., D., V., Bl. 40.

object: three columns in front of the queen's headdress on the southern tower of the pylon of the shrine
site: Meroe, pyramids on the hills, Pyr. A 15
notes: Meroitic HIEROGLYPHIC type, not cursive, and largely Griffith's restoration ('It is perhaps not too fanciful to restore the inscription thus'): only the lower part of the three columns survives. Signs he restores (above the half-brackets) are in brackets here and are not counted; '[.]' is his row of dots. Columns in reading order, right (his 'first column', compare nos. 3, 4) to left (his 'third'); each read top to bottom with side-by-side signs right to left, the rule that gives the names correctly. Middle: the cartouche of Amanishakheto. Left: asoreyi 'O Osiris', followed by three Egyptian ankh signs ('living', not transcribed); Griffith suggests 'wosi' in place of his restored te in this column. His rendering of the whole: 'Victory to the arm of Amani-shakhete, O Osiris, living.' The '?' marks are his. The pair order in the right column is not checked by any name. L., D., V., Bl. 40; Breasted photo 603; original compared.

object: demotic labels over the three large figures offering, north side of the shrine
site: Meroe, pyramids on the hills, Pyr. A 27
notes: Partial: cursive type for one group only. Griffith prints no full text of 57 (a: four lines, b: two lines, c: one line, illegible; LD VI Bl. 8 nos. 33-34; Pl. XXIX), only this group, 'consort of a king (?)', which also occurs in Kar. He adds that an isolated ḫ written below the 3-shaped letter may be a correction of it, so that sign is marked uncertain here. The group matches the corpus spelling qoresmle.

object: cartouches on the shrine (Meroitic name of the king beside an Egyptian prenomen)
site: Meroe, pyramids on the hills, Pyr. A 27
notes: Meroitic HIEROGLYPHIC type, not cursive; read with Griffith's sign table (MI I p. 49), outside the tested cursive skill. Griffith prints the Meroitic cartouche of 58 (a) inside his discussion of no. 59, as one horizontal line read right to left; hatched signs are lost, and the first two are in his brackets. He says the cartouche is incomplete at the top and more injured than when Lepsius saw it; that 'r' can readily be restored in the gap before i; that the a of Amani is omitted in the cartouche; and that the cartouche agrees closely with the name of the deceased on the altar no. 59 ('Tame(?)qêraze-Amani'). The Egyptian prenomen cartouche (copied from Sesostris I or Nekhtnebef) is not transcribed. (b) six lines on a tablet and (c) three lines are not printed in type (L., D., VI., Bl. 8, nos. 35, 36). Pl. XXX.

object: rectangular sandstone altar with spout (Berlin 2254)
site: Meroe, pyramids on the hills, Pyr. A 27
text_std: tm?lloorde? amnim?ol?wi : arqtñmkse arotnide atẖem?eẖ?lw : trekete yermlolw : twdkete ḫm?lolw : ẖolke?te
notes: Cursive type, late transition style ('lettering faulty'). Griffith prints the text in parts, joined here in this order: the name of the deceased (p. 81, over two lines), the mother's name, the father's name, then formulae K, L, C (row '59' of his table, p. 82). The opening 'O Isis, O Osiris' and the words for 'born of' and 'begotten of' are given in English only. Griffith: 'Tame(?)qêraze-Amani, truly (?) born of Araqataññimkas, begotten of Arêtanize'. He says the name has faults: its '//l' should be '//q', and its m?ol?wi (his '4ƃϟ/ʒ') is for qewi, the usual appendage. All '?' marks are Griffith's. The 3-shaped signs of formula K were checked at 2.4x (two wide ẖ, one narrow m).

object: square sandstone altar with spout (Berlin 2255)
site: Meroe, pyramids on the hills, Pyr. A 28
text_std: tkidemni atẖem?ẖelw : ptrekete : yermlolw : ptwdkete : ḫmlot : lot : e?d? : p?ẖolkete :
notes: Meroitic HIEROGLYPHIC type, not cursive; read with Griffith's sign table (MI I p. 49), outside the tested cursive skill, and cross-checked against the cursive formulae of no. 59 in the same table. Given here: the name of the deceased (Griffith: 'the honoured (?) Takizemane, born of Napata-zakhetê, begotten of Azeqetali'), then formulae K, L, C (row '60' of his table). The parents' names appear in English only and are not transcribed. The '?' marks are Griffith's; he also marks the divider after d as uncertain (written ':' here). Three reed signs in L are read as y. Griffith: 'In 60 the reading was only obtained after endless examinations'.

object: fragment of a large green-glazed plaque with whitish body, ornament in relief, probably from a table of offerings (Berlin 2138)
site: Meroe, pyramids on the hills, Pyr. A 28 (Pl. XXXII)
notes: Cursive type, archaic: six characters incised before firing on a raised band, broken at the beginning (Griffith's '['). He suggests they come from terminal formula C in the form ':wi[ḫmlol] [te]kloẖ' read right to left, i.e. [ḫmlol]wi : ẖolkte (cf. nos. 59, 60). The stroke of the te is his restoration ('[/]<-'), so te is marked uncertain; the '?' on w is his. The ẖ was checked at 2.4x (wide, angular). Griffith: 'of great importance as evidence for dating the hieroglyphic altar'.

object: royal cartouche on the northern tower of the pylon (the negro king grasping prisoners)
site: Meroe, pyramids on the hills, Pyr. A 31
notes: Meroitic HIEROGLYPHIC type, not cursive; read with Griffith's sign table (MI I p. 49), outside the tested cursive skill. Griffith prints one cartouche for nos. 62 and 63 ('The cartouches appear now to give ...'), read right to left; so 62 and 63 carry the same text. The hatched sign is lost; the '?' on d is his. Lepsius's copy of the southern cartouche had lion, man, water, reed, duck in the middle part (l i n e k), 'but in each there seem to be traces of' the eye; Griffith concludes 'the reading was therefore probably with' eye, man, water, reed, duck, 'giving the name as Tarekenizal' (the lost sign is then i). L., D., V., 49; Breasted photos 651, 652. Pl. XXXII.

object: royal cartouche on the southern tower of the pylon (the negro king grasping prisoners)
site: Meroe, pyramids on the hills, Pyr. A 31
notes: Meroitic HIEROGLYPHIC type, not cursive; read with Griffith's sign table (MI I p. 49), outside the tested cursive skill. Griffith prints one cartouche for nos. 62 and 63 ('The cartouches appear now to give ...'), read right to left; so 62 and 63 carry the same text. The hatched sign is lost; the '?' on d is his. Lepsius's copy of the southern cartouche had lion, man, water, reed, duck in the middle part (l i n e k), 'but in each there seem to be traces of' the eye; Griffith concludes 'the reading was therefore probably with' eye, man, water, reed, duck, 'giving the name as Tarekenizal' (the lost sign is then i). L., D., V., 49; Breasted photos 651, 652. Pl. XXXII.

object: slab of friable red sandstone in two fragments, three short lines of large cursive (Berlin 2251), from the side of the pyramid left of the shrine roof
site: Meroe, pyramids on the hills, Pyr. A 31
notes: Cursive type, transitional; Griffith prints it in two lines. He says it is identical with no. 70 (Pyr. A 39) except for the differences he notes: a peculiar sign before the numeral 4 and the spot after it, printed in parentheses, are absent in 70 (left out here; he suggests the sign may be a variant of one in no. 76). Numerals 3 and 4 are written as digits (strokes in the type). Griffith: the first word is the name Zamakte; ḫlbi occurs at Kalabsha (no. 94) and may be an official's title; qen is a known collocation; 'ske' is preferable to 'mke' here (his '?' on s). The k of 'kerlo' has the flat-topped k form, the same as in dmkte (checked at 2x against the table's p and k). Probably already in the corpus: T0219 ('dmkte qo xlbi 3 dime 4 kelw qe nS per lo') and T0595 ('dmkte qo xlbi 3 dime 24 kelw q nS per lo') look like this text and its duplicate no. 70; they have p where Griffith's type has k, and the same numerals.

object: slab of friable coarse red sandstone sculptured with the lowest row of an offering scene; inscription in front of the first of two small women (Berlin 2250)
site: Meroe, pyramids on the hills, Pyr. A 36
text_std: qo : sirl?mroke : lẖ : ds?lebe?te : lo : tqoroyeqo :
notes: Cursive type, later style; two printed lines; Griffith: 'The inscription is complete.' qo is a common introduction for names, perhaps honorific; lẖ is appended to names and titles; ds?lebe?te seems possible, perhaps a place-name; lo is for lowi, separated from its word as in Kar. 63; the woman's name is the last word, Taqerêye (tqoroye + qo). The '?' marks are Griffith's. The 3-shaped signs were checked at 2.2x against the table: m in sirl?mroke, ẖ in lẖ, s in sirl?mroke and ds?lebe?te.

object: royal cartouche in the shrine (one of the two walls; nos. 66 and 67 are the cartouches of the north and south walls, those of the south wall now Berlin 2269)
site: Meroe, pyramids on the hills, Pyr. A 38
notes: Meroitic HIEROGLYPHIC type, not cursive; read with Griffith's sign table (MI I p. 49), outside the tested cursive skill. Griffith prints one text for both: 'The cartouches are alike on the north and south walls', so 66 and 67 carry the same reading. He renders them 'The King of the Upper and Lower country, Lord of the two lands, Nibmare Amani-tenmêmize'; the Egyptian titles and the prenomen cartouche (copied from Amenhotep III) are not transcribed, only the Meroitic personal-name cartouche, read right to left (Amani written without its initial a). Pl. XXXIV.

object: royal cartouche in the shrine (the other wall; nos. 66 and 67 are the cartouches of the north and south walls, those of the south wall now Berlin 2269)
site: Meroe, pyramids on the hills, Pyr. A 38
notes: Meroitic HIEROGLYPHIC type, not cursive; read with Griffith's sign table (MI I p. 49), outside the tested cursive skill. Griffith prints one text for both: 'The cartouches are alike on the north and south walls', so 66 and 67 carry the same reading. He renders them 'The King of the Upper and Lower country, Lord of the two lands, Nibmare Amani-tenmêmize'; the Egyptian titles and the prenomen cartouche (copied from Amenhotep III) are not transcribed, only the Meroitic personal-name cartouche, read right to left (Amani written without its initial a). Pl. XXXIV.

object: fragments of glazed terracotta altars or tables of offerings (Khartoum Museum, from Budge's excavations)
site: Meroe, pyramids on the hills (a: from A 15; b: probably A 6; c: perhaps A 10)
text_std: [.]qore : ar[.] : ḫwit[.] woste a[.] at mlo p? n[.]ḫn
notes: Partial, several fragments. (a) Altar in blue glaze with red body, late style: two fragments, '[.]qore : ar[.]' and ': ḫwit[.]'. Griffith: the title of king (here applied to the queen?), with parts probably of the names of her father and mother, Ar... and Khaweta...; the order of the two fragments is not known. (b) Two corners of an altar in pale green glaze, somewhat earlier style (?): 'woste a[.]' and 'at mlo p?', which per Griffith 'may contain parts of a name or description of a person, and of formula B'. His '?' on p. (c) Very obscure remains of a Meroitic hieroglyphic inscription on the raised rim of another altar, printed as a vertical column in hieroglyphic type and read here top to bottom: n[.]ḫn (outside the tested cursive skill). (d, e): no text printed. Pl. XXXV. The m of mlo and the s of woste were checked at 2x.

object: red granite stela, top edge lost, ten lines between rules (found by Crowfoot)
site: Dangêl (Dungeil), north of the Atbara, within 25 miles of the Fifth Cataract
notes: Cursive type, earlier or transition style. Griffith prints the ten stone lines with superscript line numbers 1-10 at the start of each line (two printed lines at the foot of the left column, five and a short sixth at the head of the right column); a space here marks a stone-line break unless Griffith's type runs a word across it (s[.]lw, his l. 6). Each [.] is one of Griffith's dots, not a measured count; the bracketed lost sign in l. 6 carries his '?' (the i of silw). All '?' marks are Griffith's (placed above the signs), and he also queries the divider after l. 8's second gap (written ':'). Griffith: l. 1 possibly the title ḫrpḫeñ (the type shows only ñ : ḫ : r, in that order); l. 2 apile occurs as a name at Kar., and the next word may be an old version of pelmos 'the strategus'; l. 3 qesewi occurs in Meroë no. 6, epḫ[.] looks like a word in Kar. 78; l. 6 silw occurs at Umm Soda (no. 45). He renders ll. 1-2 'Apile, kharpkheñ in ....; strategus (?) in .... (?)' and thinks at most one line is lost at the top. The 3-shaped signs were checked at 2.2x against the table: m in pe?l?i?ms?i?, pḫemlo and ml?i?li; ẖ in r?ẖe[.]w, d?iẖode and ẖot?; s in sk and bñyosit.
